# Contributing

Version: v2026.01.18 • Author: 7Lynx

Thanks for looking at HoundMind. This project drives a robot dog, so the rules below are short on
purpose: they keep the history readable and the dog out of trouble.

## Who this applies to

Every commit, pull request, issue and comment in `seven-lynx/HoundMind`, including contributions
opened from a fork. Everything is published under one human identity: commit as yourself, open the
pull request from your own fork or a branch on this repository, and leave no attribution to a tool
or a model anywhere in the text. CI fails a commit that is authored by any other account, so the rule
is enforced rather than merely documented.

## Branches and commits

- Branch: `<type>/<kebab>`, where `type` is one of `feature`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `test`,
  `refactor`, `perf`, `audit`, `build`, `ci`, `release`.
- Commit: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — `feat:`, `fix:`,
  `chore:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `test:`.
- One logical change per commit. A structure change and a behaviour change do not share a commit.
- The body explains *why*. No `[deploy]`, `[ship]`, `[prod]` or `[release]` tags.

## The language rule

Nothing in the record — a commit subject or body, a commit trailer, a pull request title or
description, a review comment, an issue, a changelog line, a code comment — describes how the text
was produced. No "generated by", no "written with", and no co-author trailer naming a tool.

## Docs ship with the change

| Change | Update in the same commit |
|---|---|
| Behaviour | `CHANGELOG.md` |
| New or changed config key | `config/settings.jsonc` comment + `docs/FEATURES_GUIDE.md` |
| New module | `README.md` feature table + `docs/FEATURES_GUIDE.md` |
| New `tools.<name>` entry point | `docs/HOUNDMIND_PROGRAMMING_GUIDE.md` or `docs/INSTALL.md` |
| Version bump | `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` together |

## Before you open a pull request

```powershell
python -m ruff check src
$env:PYTHONPATH='src'; python -m pytest -q
mypy src --ignore-missing-imports
```

CI runs the same three checks on Python 3.11, then builds the sdist and the wheel. A fourth job,
`Identity guard`, fails when a commit reaching this repository is authored by an account other than
the project's own — the local hooks only inspect the unpushed range, so this is the check that sees a
commit made elsewhere. A red run is fixed by changing the code, never by loosening the workflow.
Fill in
`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and state the motion impact — `none`, `dry-run only`, or
`commands servos`.

The test suite runs with no hardware attached. Reach for `hal/fake.py::FakeDogHAL` rather than a
device, and put anything that needs a real Pi in `src/tools/`.

## Motion

Nothing in this repository commands the dog on your behalf. A check or a test that moves a servo is
opt-in and off by default, and is only run with the dog on the ground and clear of anything it
could break. A pull request that moves the dog is reviewed as high risk by definition.

## Secrets

Never commit a device token, WiFi credential, API key or a stream URL that embeds one. The device
token lives outside the repository, in `~/.houndmind/api_token`.
